problem.title: Process Tasks Using Servers
problem.summary:
You are given two 0-indexed integer arrays `servers` and `tasks` of lengths `n`​​​​​​ and `m`​​​​​​ respectively. `servers[i]` is the weight of the `i​​​​​​th`​​​​ server, and `tasks[j]` is the time needed to process the `j​​​​​​th`​​​​ task in seconds.
Tasks are assigned to the servers using a task queue. Initially, all servers are free, and the queue is empty.
At second `j`, the `jth` task is in...

solution.approach: Maintain two min-heaps: one for available servers sorted by (weight, index), and another for busy servers sorted by (free_time, weight, index). Advance time to process each task chronologically.
solution.code:
import heapq

class Solution:
    def assignTasks(self, servers: list[int], tasks: list[int]) -> list[int]:
        # Two priority queues: free servers (weight, index) and busy servers (available_time, weight, index)
        free = [(w, i) for i, w in enumerate(servers)]
        heapq.heapify(free)
        busy = []
        ans = []
        time = 0
        
        for i, task_time in enumerate(tasks):
            time = max(time, i)
            # If no free servers, jump time forward to next available server
            if not free and busy and busy[0][0] > time:
                time = busy[0][0]
                
            while busy and busy[0][0] <= time:
                _, weight, idx = heapq.heappop(busy)
                heapq.heappush(free, (weight, idx))
                
            weight, idx = heapq.heappop(free)
            ans.append(idx)
            heapq.heappush(busy, (time + task_time, weight, idx))
            
        return ans
solution.verification_notes: Passed all 2 verified example test cases.
solution.hint: Use two priority queues to separate available servers from busy ones and advance time when idle.
